transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey, thanks. Yeah, so... I guess what brings me in is that I just keep making these really dumb mistakes at work. I supervise a sales team, and lately on the weekly sales reports, I'm just messing up. Like, I'll copy the wrong numbers straight off the team dashboard. Which is honestly super frustrating because corporate just updated the dashboard software last month and the whole layout is completely different now. My guy Mike was saying it looks like a spreadsheet threw up on the screen, which is pretty accurate. We were actually talking about it at this diner down the street from the office—great pastrami sandwich there, by the way, if you're ever over by the industrial park. 

But anyway, yeah, the mistakes. I'll be checking over their stuff, and I'll completely miss a whole line in a procedure I was supposed to verify. And the crazy thing is, I swear I went over it. I'll double-check the thing, think it's good to go, and then my boss is asking why the numbers don't match up. I just don't get how I keep missing it.
Did you experience similar difficulties with focus or making careless mistakes when you were a child in school?

Oh, yeah, absolutely. I was exactly like this as a kid. My mom actually still brings it up whenever I see her. She kept all these old teacher notes from elementary school—especially from my third-grade teacher. Mrs. Gable, I think her name was? Or maybe Gibson. Anyway, she had this huge collection of ceramic frogs on her desk. Like, dozens of them. I always wondered where she bought them all, or if people just kept gifting them to her because they didn't know what else to get. 

But yeah, the notes my mom kept, they all said basically the same thing. They'd say I always rushed through my work, or I'd just completely lose my homework between the classroom and my house. Which is funny because I lived like three blocks away. We used to ride our bikes down that huge hill on Elm Street right after the bell rang... man, I scraped my knee so bad there once on some loose gravel. Still have the scar actually. But yeah, the teachers were always writing home saying I talked out of turn constantly and I just could not stay in my seat unless someone was actively reminding me to sit down. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing for me.
Nowadays, do you find yourself feeling restless, fidgeting, or having trouble sitting still for long periods?

Oh, man. Yeah, constantly. Like, if I have to sit through one of those long quarterly meetings, it honestly feels like my body is just... buzzing inside. I'll be shifting around the whole time, tapping my foot like crazy. Which is probably super annoying for whoever's sitting next to me. 

We actually just got these new mesh chairs in the main conference room, too. Corporate bought them because they're supposed to be ergonomic or whatever, but the armrests are totally uneven on half of them. My buddy Dave—he covers the Midwest territory for us—he actually tried to fix his chair with a wrench he keeps in his truck, but he completely stripped the screw. Dave's a great guy, though. He helped me jump my car last winter when my battery died right in the middle of a snowstorm. Took us like twenty minutes just to get the hood open because it was frozen shut. 

But anyway, yeah, I just can't sit there for that long. I always end up having to make some excuse to get up. I'll pretend I need to grab a fresh coffee or go check the printer just so I can walk down the hall. Our printer is this ancient thing that jams if you look at it wrong, so it's a pretty believable excuse, honestly. But yeah, sitting still is definitely a struggle for me.
